findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Inspector observed that the bottom of the 2 door cooler has some spilled liquids. CORRECTED: PIC was aware and plans to clean the spill soon, as the cooler has already been sold to another facility after the end of the school year. Ensure that nonfood-contact surfaces are kept from from an accumulation of residue and other debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed boxes of single-use articles (i.e., cups, lids) stored directly on the ground in the storage closet outside of the kitchen. The PIC was educated that all single-use articles must be stored at least 6-inches above the ground to avoid contamination. Ensure proper storage by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed an employee did not use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing. The inspector educated the employee and they re-washed hands using the proper hand washing procedure. Ensure that a barrier is always used to turn off the faucet after hand washing. 

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed there was not paper towels at the hand sink when the inspector arrived. The PIC provided the hand sink with paper towels during the inspection. Ensure there is always paper towels available at the hand washing sink.

6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Observed boxes of food (including, but not limited too, cans of peaches, pears, and granola bars) stored on the floor in the closets. The inspector educated the PIC about storing food at least 6-inches off the floor to protect against contamination. Ensure that food is stored at least 6-inches above the floor by the next routine inspection.

3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Observed wet wiping cloths stored in the triple sink not in sanitizer solution. In-use wiping cloths must be stored in chemical sanitizer between uses. The inspector educated the employee and the wet wiping cloths were removed for laundering. Ensure that wet wiping cloths are always stored in chemical solution between uses and laundered daily.

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the following items to be in need of repair/replacement/sealing to create surfaces which are smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable:
- the far right cabinet door underneath the sinks is improperly hung which has created a gap along the upper edge of the cabinet allow entry of water and other materials into the cabinet itself.
- the caulking/plastic liner along the back of the counter is no longer attached and there is a gap allowing entry of water and other materials into the space behind the cabinets.
- the corner cabinet in the lower portion of cabinets is damaged leaving exposed bare wood and a non-functional door.
- the far left corner of the cabinets closest to the entryway from the cafeteria to the kitchen has corners which have been damaged from use and exposed bare wood is present.
- the base coving to the left of the door was attached with a small nail which has come loose from the wall allowing the coving itself to pull away from the wall.

Ensure that these items are repaired/sealed to create surfaces which are smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable and ensure that operators are aware of the requirements for surfaces in the facility and report items in need of repair/replacement/sealing as often as necessary. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
findings.comment: No hand wash station is installed in proximity to kitchen.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.comment: Outer openings not protected from insects, rodent proof

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment: 750-120(a) (1) Observed personal food for employees stored intermingled with food for the children. Personal food shall be stored separate from food for the children. Store personal food down and way from food for the children or in a separate unit. (2) Observed single service containers re-used to store food for the children. Cease to use single service containers for food storage. Facility shall use food grade plastics to protect food. Food shall be protected at all times during storage.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment: 750-880 Observed  plastic spoons and single service trays stored on the floor in the dry storage closet. Single service items shall be protected at all times during storage. Store single service items at least six (6) inches from the floor.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.comment: There are no thermometers in the cold holding units or the hot holding unit. 750.140(a) All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F. Provide thermometers for these three units.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: Upon arrival there are trays draining on dish towels and mats. Also there is an absorbent cloth in the cabinet on the shelf holding the plastic glasses. 750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition. The cloth was removed and the facility will provide drain racks for proper air drying of dishes. Cabinet cloth was removed and shelf sanitized for glasses to be replaced.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: The wash cloth for the dishes and wet wiping is observed to be sitting on the counter. 750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses. A sanitizer bucket was prepared and used.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: The base cabinet under the sink has soil and two dead roaches. 750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris. Clean and maintain clean.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
The facility has areas where walls need to be sealed: 1. Seal the walls behind the hand sinks in the rest rooms. 2.  Repair the wall in the one restroom where cove and nudo is missing. 3. Seal the walls where they are  in contact with the counter tops in the kitchen and 4.  seal wall around pipes in the base cabinet under the dink in the kitchen.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.comment: Upon arrival a purse is observed in cabinet that contains breakfast cereal. 750-1280 Adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings. Move purse to cabinet with other non food items or items intended to be maintained clean.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.comment: Milk cooler does not have a thermometer. Provide a thermometer for this cooler.
findings.citation_text: 750.140(a) All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Observed kitchen staff cutting fruit without gloves on. Wash hands and wear gloves to prevent bare hand contact with ready to eat foods.
750-160 Ready to eat foods shall be handled in a manner to minimize direct hand contact.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
1) REPEAT> Observed a gap in the back of the sink and the wall in the restroom nearest the kitchen. 2) Observed shelves in the dry storage closet to be made of bare wood. Seal or paint wood so that it is smooth, nonabsorbent and easily cleanable.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
Observed the restroom nearest the kitchen to not have a self closer. Provide self closer for restroom door.
750-1120 All restrooms must have self-closing doors, properly operating fixtures, be clean and have proper hand washing supplies in order to help facilitate good hygienic practices.  Provide properly designed and maintained restrooms.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: Observed a gap in the back of the sink and the wall in the restroom nearest the kitchen--750.690 Seal the gap(caulk).

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
750-1120 All restrooms must have self-closing doors, properly operating fixtures, be clean and have proper hand washing supplies in order to help facilitate good hygienic practices. 
The employee restrooms do not have self closers on the doors.
Provide properly designed and maintained restrooms.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  
Some floor tiles in the kitchen area are chipped on their corners.
Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
750-1210(b) Walls and ceilings in walk-in refrigeration units, food prepartion areas, equipment washing areas, and toilet rooms shall be smooth, light-cored, non-absorbant, and easily cleanable. Concrete or pumice block in these locations shall be finished and sealed to provide a cleanable surface.
There are ceiling tiles in the employee bathrooms that are perforated-type, instead of smooth-surface.
Repair tiles in rest rooms.
